title: Add up a bill with recursion
prompt:
Write `total(prices)` so it adds up a list of prices by calling itself. No loops and no `sum()` this time.

Think of it as nested dolls. The total of an empty list is 0: that is the smallest doll, your base case. The total of any other list is its first price plus the total of the rest of the list: open one doll and hand the rest to a smaller copy of the same job.

When it works, `python3 total.py` prints `8.0` and then `0`.
hints: Start with the base case. If `prices == []`, give back 0 right away.
`prices[0]` is the first price. `prices[1:]` is a new list with everything after it.
The recursive case is one line: `return prices[0] + total(prices[1:])`.
explain_after: A function that calls itself is recursive [py-139], and the condition that stops it is the base case [py-142]. Each call to `total` gets its own frame with its own `prices`, one frame per call [py-140], and each list is one price shorter than the last. When the empty list arrives, the base case answers 0 and the frames hand their sums back down the tower.
